model_guides.title: Change engine oil and filter
steps: Warm the engine 2 minutes, then shut it off and park on level ground.
Raise the vehicle safely on ramps or jack stands.
Remove the drain plug and let the oil drain into the pan.
Remove the old filter (cartridge-style spin-on filter under the front of the engine), oil the new gasket and fit it hand-tight.
Refit the drain plug with a new gasket and torque to spec.
Fill with 6 qt of 5W-30, run 30 s, check for leaks, recheck the dipstick.
Reset the oil-life monitor in the instrument cluster menu.
model_guides.source: assumption: drafted from the 2019 Ford F-150 owner manual and maintenance schedule; needs a person's check

model_guides.title: Replace engine air filter
steps: Open the hood and find the air box next to the engine.
Release the clips on the air box lid.
Lift out the old filter and wipe debris from the box.
Seat the new filter with the rubber edge all the way round.
Close the lid and lock every clip.
model_guides.source: assumption: drafted from the 2019 Ford F-150 owner manual and maintenance schedule; needs a person's check

model_guides.title: Replace cabin air filter
steps: Open the glove box, release the stops, and remove the filter cover behind it.
Slide out the old filter and note the airflow arrow.
Insert the new filter with the arrow pointing the same way.
Refit the cover or glove box.
model_guides.source: assumption: drafted from the 2019 Ford F-150 owner manual and maintenance schedule; needs a person's check

model_guides.title: Rotate tires
steps: Loosen the lug nuts a half turn on all four wheels.
Raise the vehicle and support it on jack stands.
Move the wheels front-to-rear on the same side (rearward cross for 4WD trucks).
Hand-tighten, lower, then torque the lug nuts in a star pattern.
Set all tires to 35 psi cold, per the door-jamb placard.
model_guides.source: assumption: drafted from the 2019 Ford F-150 owner manual and maintenance schedule; needs a person's check

model_guides.title: Replace wiper blades
steps: Lift the wiper arm off the windshield.
Press the release tab and slide the old blade off the hook.
Slide the new blade on until it clicks.
Lower the arm gently and test the wipers.
model_guides.source: assumption: drafted from the 2019 Ford F-150 owner manual and maintenance schedule; needs a person's check

model_guides.title: Test and replace the 12V battery
steps: With the engine off for an hour, measure the battery: 12.6 V is full, below 12.2 V is weak.
Disconnect the negative terminal first, then the positive.
Remove the hold-down and lift the battery out.
Clean the terminals, fit the new battery and the hold-down.
Connect positive first, then negative. Most parts stores recycle the old battery.
model_guides.source: assumption: drafted from the 2019 Ford F-150 owner manual and maintenance schedule; needs a person's check

model_guides.title: Replace front brake pads
steps: Raise the front and remove the wheels.
Remove the caliper bolts and hang the caliper; never let it hang by the hose.
Remove the old pads, check rotor thickness against the minimum stamped on it.
Push the piston back, fit the new pads with grease on the contact points.
Refit the caliper and torque the bolts, refit the wheels.
Pump the brake pedal until firm before driving, then bed in the pads with gentle stops.
model_guides.source: assumption: drafted from the 2019 Ford F-150 owner manual and maintenance schedule; needs a person's check

model_guides.title: Check 2.7L EcoBoost oil consumption and PCV
steps: Check the dipstick at every fill-up for 1,000 mi and log the level.
More than 1 qt per 3,000 mi is excessive; note any blue smoke at start-up.
Inspect the PCV hose and valve on the driver side for oil residue or cracks.
Look for oil seeping at the composite oil pan seam.
Bring the log to a Ford dealer: a leaking oil pan or PCV fault may be covered by the 5 yr / 60k powertrain warranty.
model_guides.source: assumption: drafted from the 2019 Ford F-150 owner manual and maintenance schedule; needs a person's check

model_guides.title: Spot Dynamic Fuel Management lifter trouble
steps: Listen at idle for a steady ticking from the top of the engine that rises with RPM.
Note any misfire, check-engine light, or rough idle at low speed.
Scan for codes P0300 to P0308 (misfires) and P3400-range cylinder deactivation codes.
Do not keep driving with a flashing check-engine light.
This repair (lifters, sometimes camshaft) is shop-only; ask whether the 5 yr / 60k powertrain warranty covers it.

model_guides.title: Fix a dead 12V battery on the RAV4 Hybrid
steps: A dead 12V battery means the car will not show READY; the hybrid battery is usually fine.
Open the hood and jump from the 12V battery terminals as the owner manual shows.
Once READY, leave it on for 30 minutes; the hybrid system charges the 12V battery.
If it dies again within days, test it: below 12.4 V after a night parked means replace with an AGM battery.
Avoid leaving accessories or a dashcam on while the car is off.
model_guides.source: assumption: drafted from the 2021 Toyota RAV4 Hybrid owner manual and maintenance schedule; needs a person's check
